round1_to_round2.convergence_assessment: This is mostly anchoring, not independent agreement. (1) The round-2 mean ladder is almost identical to my round-1 ladder (P>=838 0.492 vs my 0.497; P>=1005 0.357 vs 0.365). (2) Every agent now builds NTM EPS at Oct-2027 from the CY2028 contract-pricing cases my feedback proposed. Agent 3 uses exactly the -5%/flat/+10% grid I suggested, agents 1 and 5 use the same 30/50/20 weights, and the five NTM EPS figures ($43-48) bracket my $47. (3) Agent 4 justifies 17x with 'the supervisor also lands at 17x'. Agent 2 sets its FCF yield 'between my round-1 4.5% and the 5% cross-check'. All five add $6-8 per share of net cash after my ~$8. (4) In source_overlap, mean Jaccard doubled from 0.106 to 0.216 and distinct share fell from 0.734 to 0.609. The four URLs newly cited by 3+ agents (transcript, Sep-8 8-K, Investing.com/Nikkei, mreport Toshiba roadmap) all came from my round-1 source list, and several agents label them 'via supervisor'. The factual convergence is legitimate: debt about $2.4B, about 230M shares, volume allocated into CY2028, pricing set only for CY2027, and the Toshiba FY2027 timing are verified primaries. The convergence of judgment (multiples, case weights, net cash) is not new evidence, so I count about 2-3 effective independent views, not 5. There were real independent pushbacks: agent 1 on the one-off pricing (it is right), agent 5 on 16.5x, agent 4 on a 6% yield, agent 2 on a $500 break. New independent evidence: agent 5's Kalshi pull and agent 4's tracker data. Research effort this round was thin (1-4 queries per agent).

disagreements.topic: NTM EPS at Oct-2027 (CY2028 contract-pricing cases)
disagreements.positions: Agent 1 $47.5 (flat $41 30% / modest $48 50% / strong $56 20%); agent 2 FY28 $47 plus a flat case at $38; agent 3 ~$43 (-5%/flat/+10% at 30/35/35, cases $37.5/$41/$47); agent 4 $48 (flat to +5%); agent 5 $46 (flat/down $38 30% / $47 50% / $55 20%).
disagreements.resolution: The flat-pricing cases are built too low. The Q4 call gives a mid-20% exabyte growth target. If price per EB is flat in CY2028, revenue still grows with exabytes, roughly 5% a quarter, and higher HAMR mix lowers cost per TB. So 'flat price' does not mean 'flat EPS'. From a Q4 FY27 run-rate of about $9.2-9.8 with about 6% quarterly EPS growth and no price increase, NTM (FQ2'28-FQ1'29) comes to about $45-46, not $38-41. Agent 1 explicitly assumed 'flat units' with only cost gains, and agent 3 'holds the run-rate'. A real bear needs price per EB to fall back to the old -5 to -10% a year, or exabyte demand to stall, which gives about $40-42. Re-weighted on the agents' own probabilities, NTM EPS is about $48 (range $40-56), not the $46 mean. This is my arithmetic on guided inputs, not a searched fact. Its value impact is about +$25-30 per share at 16.5-17x, but it remains contingent on mid-20s exabyte demand holding into 2028.
disagreements.evidence: Seagate Q4 FY26 corrected transcript: 'support our mid-20% exabyte growth target'; 'contracts that define both product configuration and pricing terms, covering the entirety of calendar 2027'; 'every quarter revenue to improve and every quarter gross margin'.

disagreements.topic: Was part of the September price-per-EB jump one-off? (agent 3 vs agent 1, and my round-1 wording)
disagreements.positions: Agent 3 puts FY27 in the low half ($33.5) because part of the September jump was a one-off (preferential HAMR customer rolling off). Agent 1 pushes back: the CFO called it minor. My round-1 file stressed the one-off.
disagreements.resolution: Agent 1 is right, and my round-1 emphasis was overstated. The CFO: 'the volume that was sold at the preferential price in June was minimal... a little bit of a positive impact... But is not the major reason why pricing is a little bit better in September than June. Of course, there's more overall demand.' The call does show one genuinely opportunistic element: extra output from yield gains is being sold 'at a very good price right now', and 'every quarter is different'. That argues against extrapolating the ~20% YoY September price/EB, not for a lower FY27. The effect is below about $0.5 of FY27 EPS. FY27 stays at about $33-35.
disagreements.evidence: Q4 FY26 corrected transcript, Q&A (CFO Romano; CEO Mosley: 'We are pretty predictable, I think, through FY 2027').

disagreements.topic: Multiple and FCF yield at the horizon
disagreements.resolution: No search can settle this; it is judgment. The two dispersions largely offset inside each agent: agent 3's 18x pairs with the lowest EPS, and agent 4's 6% yield with a 0.95 FCF conversion. I use 16.5-17x and 5% (peak-cycle earnings with open CY2028 pricing, against 8-15x HDD peak history). Agent 4's 0.95 conversion contradicts its own 0.88 FY26 figure. At 0.87 its FCF leg falls from $770 to about $705 at 6% (about $845 at 5%), and its fair value to about $772. The leg is internally inconsistent and should be restated.
disagreements.evidence: Q4 FY26 release/call: FY26 FCF $3.1B on ~$3.54B non-GAAP net income (~0.87); capex 4-6% of revenue.

disagreements.topic: Net cash at the horizon and share count
disagreements.positions: All five add +$1.5-2B net cash (~$6-8 per share) and hold about 229-230M shares.
disagreements.resolution: The two assumptions are inconsistent. From net debt of about $0.6B today, the next four quarters' FCF (about $7B on about $37 EPS at 0.87 conversion) less about $0.7B of dividends leaves about +$5.5-6B (~$25 per share) if nothing is bought back. The agents reach only +$1.8-2B by assuming about $4B of buybacks, but at about $830 that retires about 5M shares (~2%), which none of them deducts. Either way, the per-share value of the cash build is about $15-25, not $6-8. That is a +$10-15 per share understatement in every agent's fair value.
disagreements.evidence: Q4 FY26 call ('retiring an additional $1.2 billion in debt' in the Sep quarter; gross debt ~$3.6B at FYE); Sep-8 8-K; 10-K ($4.8B buyback authorization, cited by agent 1).

disagreements.positions: Round 1: 41% from an aggregator (discounted). Round 2: agent 5 pulled 22c from Kalshi's public API.
disagreements.resolution: Verified on 2026-10-02 from api.elections.kalshi.com: KXRECSSNBER-27 last $0.22, previous $0.22, bid $0.20 / ask $0.22, open interest ~275k. Two corrections. (a) 'Volume ~$542k' is 542,225 contracts (volume_fp counts contracts), so the dollar value traded is much lower, about $0.1M at ~20c, and 24-hour volume was only ~3.8k contracts. (b) The rule is two consecutive negative advance-estimate GDP quarters within Q4-2026 to Q4-2027, a narrower bar than an NBER recession (the 2026 contract trades at 6c). It is a legitimate, moderately liquid macro input and supports agent 5's cut in bust weight from 25% to 22%. But STX's main risk is an industry supply/pricing cycle, not a GDP recession, so I do not move the ladder further on it.

disagreements.positions: Agent 4: street $/TB still rising with no plateau (eRacks, published 2026-09-14), and a renewed Exos 24TB at $749.99 on 2026-10-02 vs $699 on 2026-08-28.
disagreements.resolution: Partly verified, and weak for CY2028 contract pricing. The eRacks release exists and says what agent 4 reports. Mar-Aug: Barracuda +92%, Toshiba MG +38%, Exos SATA +15%, 'nothing fell'. But it is a small vendor's own marketing release, covering retail and channel street prices only through August, before the Toshiba news, and the enterprise Exos line moved least. Agent 2 cites the same release, so it is one source, not two. On the datacenterdisk page the $749.99 is a single third-party Amazon 'Renewed' listing, which the site itself rates 'FAIR PRICE' against its own history. The page has no $699 data point; that figure comes from a different source (a Yahoo Tech article). So the comparison is cross-source, not a like-for-like series. The same page shows a comparable renewed WD 24TB at $669 ($27.88/TB) as the cheapest refurbished 24TB. Conclusion: no sign that spot pricing has rolled over, but no evidence of fresh acceleration either. This should not move the ladder.

Kept at $520, about 11x my $48 NTM EPS. Agent 4's $560 is a reasonable early-warning level, and agent 2's $500 is defensible because the 2018/2022 drawdowns began only after pricing rolled over. No new evidence separates them.

summary: STX closed at $837.52 after an 11% drop on the Toshiba capacity report. Round 2 narrowed the forecasters' fair values to $770-815 (mean $794), but mostly by anchoring on my round-1 framework rather than through new independent evidence. My checks verified agent 5's Kalshi 22% (with volume in contracts, not dollars), found agent 4's new tracker data real but too weak to move the forecast, and confirmed agent 1's correction that the September one-off pricing effect was minor. The one substantive change is arithmetic: the agents' 'flat CY2028 pricing' cases drop the guided mid-20s exabyte growth and understate the cash build. That lifts my fair value to about $820 (about 2% below spot) and the middle of the ladder by about a point. The multiple paid for peak earnings and CY2028 contract pricing remain unresolved, so confidence is low. With about 70% volatility there is no clear Sharpe edge over the S&P 500.

sizing.conviction_label_reason: Even after the upward correction, fair value (~$820) sits at or just below spot, and with about 70% realized vol, an unresolved peak-cycle multiple and CY2028 pricing risk, there is no checked edge in expected return over the S&P 500 to act on.

sizing.reason: STX is a high-volatility cyclical at a likely earnings peak, with a supply headline still unresolved and an earnings report within four weeks. It shares the AI-capex driver with three of the five holdings. A 4% cap (about $400 of the ~$9,961 portfolio, which already includes the cash) limits a 40-60% cyclical drawdown to about 2% of the portfolio. My simulation of the Sharpe comparison, with the stock's median near spot and 0.5 correlation to SPY, gives about 0.42-0.44, so I put confidence at 0.42.
